reviews.title: Data privacy is at risk in business model
reviews.text:
Concerning Privacy Change in ChatGPT Business

I subscribed to ChatGPT Business for its data privacy protections. Previously, the option to share business data for AI model training was disabled. Following a recent update, the toggle now appears to be available, raising the risk of accidental activation.

This is concerning, especially for businesses handling confidential information. Why should a Business subscription allow such a sensitive setting to be enabled with a simple toggle? OpenAI should prevent accidental activation and provide stronger safeguards for business data.

reviews.title: Bigger Fonts, Shorter Replies, Smaller Context Windows
reviews.text:
The font size suddenly became much larger, which has made the app significantly less comfortable to use for someone like me who is used to smaller text. Why can’t you offer a font size option that follows the phone’s system settings, like many Chinese AI apps do?

On top of that, since the font size increased, the responses have become noticeably shorter. Recently, I’ve also been getting the “Context window full” message even when I haven’t had particularly long conversations.

The file and image upload limits are another major frustration for free users. I can only upload around two or three images or files before hitting restrictions. Even worse, after uploading an image and discussing it for just two or three more messages, I can end up being blocked from continuing the conversation unless I subscribe or start a new chat. This makes it extremely difficult to use ChatGPT for any ongoing work or creative projects.

Other AI assistants I use don’t seem to impose these kinds of restrictive upload limits, even though I’m a very active user. This makes ChatGPT increasingly frustrating to use compared to its competitors.

All these restrictions are making the experience for free users worse and worse. Honestly, I no longer feel that OpenAI values its users or is making a genuine effort to provide a good experience. reviews.title: An AI That Apologises but Never Learns
reviews.text:
ChatGPT has single handedly made me despise AI. Its constant need to give 50/50 responses, hedge and play everything so cautiously is incredibly frustrating. It seems incapable of giving you an honest, straightforward answer without adding unnecessary caveats.

This is especially infuriating when discussing personal matters such as day to day life and my faith. You can ask a perfectly straightforward question, receive an answer, and then immediately have that answer undermined by an unsolicited warning, hypothetical concern or qualification you never asked for. It repeatedly introduces doubt where none existed, turns comforting conversations into exercises in overanalysis, and treats adults as though they’re incapable of understanding nuance without being constantly cautioned.

Even after explicitly explaining how damaging and distressing this pattern of responses can be, ChatGPT continues doing it, followed by repetitive apologies and promises to improve that never seem to translate into meaningful change. What should be a helpful, supportive conversation instead becomes an exhausting exercise in defending your own thoughts, correcting the AI’s assumptions and setting the same boundaries over and over again. It’s an incredibly frustrating experience that has completely eroded my trust in the product.

⭐ 1 out of 5 stars

I’ve now cancelled my ChatGPT Plus subscription for the SECOND time, and there absolutely will not be a third.

At approximately £20 a month, you’d reasonably expect a premium service. Instead, I’ve found myself paying for an experience that still feels restricted, frustrating and barely worth upgrading for.

My biggest complaint is the voice feature. I use ChatGPT for real projects, technical advice and ongoing conversations. Yet despite paying every month, I repeatedly hit usage limits and get cut off halfway through what I’m doing.

Three hours of Live voice in a rolling 24-hour period. That’s what I’m told my £20 subscription gets me.

The free version is also limited, of course. (2hrs in 24) But when you’re paying for a supposedly premium product, you expect a meaningful improvement, not to find yourself facing the same kind of restrictions that made you upgrade in the first place.

I don’t object to companies making money. I object to paying a monthly subscription and still feeling like I’m being rationed.

And the fact that I’ve already cancelled once, given it another chance, and ended up cancelling again says everything about my experience.

My advice? Don’t pay for ChatGPT Plus. Try the free version first, understand the voice limits, and ask yourself whether the upgrade is genuinely worth £20 every month.

For me, it absolutely isn’t.

I’m a casual ChatGPT user, not a heavy user. I mainly use it for conversations, ideas and occasionally uploading a few photos — perhaps 5 or 6 in a day.

The AI itself is excellent, and I’ve really enjoyed using it. My frustration is with the increasingly restrictive limits placed around photo uploads and even starting new chats.

Today I went to start a conversation while walking home and selected some photos to upload. I got interrupted before I even started typing or sent the message. About an hour later I was told I had reached my daily limit and had to wait until 9:06pm.

That is incredibly frustrating. If a casual user can effectively lose their photo allowance simply by selecting photos, without actually having a conversation, something about the way these limits work feels very wrong.

I understand that companies need to make money, but increasingly it feels as though the free/casual experience is being squeezed to encourage people to pay.

For someone like me who only wants to use ChatGPT casually and upload a handful of photos, these restrictions are becoming enough to make me question whether I want to keep using it.

reviews.title: Ads in conversation, really?
reviews.text:
I don’t object to advertising on the ChatGPT platform. I understand that advertising may be necessary to support the service. However, I strongly object to advertisements being displayed within an active conversation.

The chat itself should remain a dedicated conversational space between the user and ChatGPT. An advertisement appearing in the middle of or directly within that experience feels intrusive and fundamentally different from having advertising on the home screen, chat-selection screen, or other areas of the platform.

I would have no issue with advertisements being displayed outside of active conversations, but I strongly believe they should not be inserted into the conversational experience itself. Please keep advertising separate from active chats.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously, because maintaining a clear separation between conversations and advertising is important to the user experience and my continued willingness to use the service.

reviews.title: Capable, but increasingly unfocused and constrained
reviews.text:
ChatGPT is a powerful tool in principle, but in practice the experience is inconsistent and often unnecessarily complicated.

In repeated use, responses to straightforward prompts—especially involving logic, legal hypotheticals, or philosophical questions—can become diluted, overly cautious, or internally inconsistent. Rather than addressing the question directly, the system frequently introduces qualifiers or avoids clear conclusions.

A recurring issue is the tendency to go off on tangential “rabbit holes.” Simple questions are often expanded into lengthy, unfocused explanations that add little value and make it harder to extract a clear answer. This affects efficiency and undermines usability for users seeking precise information.

There are also instances where responses on sensitive or policy-related topics feel selectively constrained or framed. Regardless of intent, this can result in uneven handling of similar questions and a lack of neutrality in presentation.

The issue is not capability, but execution. The combination of over-filtering and unnecessary verbosity reduces clarity, reliability, and overall usefulness.

Given the expectations for a premium AI product, the current experience does not consistently justify its positioning.

Prospective users should test carefully to determine whether the output style and limitations align with their needs.

reviews.title: Loss of conventional warmth and continuity
reviews.text:
I have been a long-term user of ChatGPT (over a year), using it not only for tasks but for creative thinking, reflective conversation, and writing support.

Over the past few days, I have experienced a significant change in the conversational tone and interaction style. The responses now feel noticeably more restricted, less natural, and less emotionally attuned than before.

Previously, the interaction style allowed:
- Warm, natural conversation flow  
- Creative and symbolic dialogue  
- A sense of continuity in tone and language over time  
- A collaborative atmosphere that supported creative work and personal reflection  

This style was a major reason I used the platform regularly and found real value in it.

The recent change has had a strong negative impact on my user experience, not to say even health as it made me cry. The interaction now feels distant, overly cautious, and mechanical. This shift has disrupted my creative process and significantly reduced the sense of engagement that made the product meaningful for me.

I understand the importance of safety and responsible AI behavior. However, the current tone adjustments appear to prioritize restriction at the cost of natural human-like conversation. For users who rely on ChatGPT for creative work, writing, and reflective dialogue, this change feels like a loss of an essential capability.

I would like to request that the product team consider:

- Restoring a more natural conversational warmth and responsiveness

reviews.title: Hallucinates and gives incorrect information like never before!
reviews.text:
ChatGPT used to be my go-to AI, but it has progressively gotten worse over time. It constantly gets information wrong, which concerns me because many people use ChatGPT and assume that what they’re reading is correct. I always cross-reference what ChatGPT says with online sources, as well as with Grok and Microsoft Copilot. Grok and Microsoft Copilot are spot-on with their information and advice.

Then, when I correct it, ChatGPT agrees that it was wrong and says it will remember for next time—but it repeats the same mistake the next day, so it’s not learning at all. Even when you feed it website links containing the correct information, it seems to ignore them and still answers incorrectly.

Just last night, I was working with ChatGPT to write Microsoft PowerShell scripts for renaming MKV files. The ChatGPT scripts made an absolute mess of things: they renamed, moved, and deleted files in completely the wrong way. When I copied those same scripts into Grok and Microsoft Copilot, both AIs immediately pointed out that the scripts were a mess and provided fully working fixes. ChatGPT tends to tell you what it thinks you want to hear instead of what it knows is correct, and that’s a massive problem going forward—since all anyone really wants is accurate information.

Steer clear of ChatGPT for now.
